doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Space and silence in the playing; Miles and Wayne Shorter
summary: Ries explains that what you leave out is powerful, citing Miles and Shorter, and says he tries to sing through the instrument like his father.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: It was clear to me that you understand the importance and the power of space and dynamics. Because there was a number of times, one time when you were playing — you played the melody to “Bye-Bye Blackbird.” And there was all those like holes in there. And you know Ron was playing a little bit behind you but I don’t hear people do that that much. And I wonder why you did it and I wondered is it because of this audience — it’s very quiet in there. And those silences, man, are very —

Well it’s often what you don’t play which is more powerful. You know? Giving that space in thought but also to allow the other musicians around to give him time to add his thing. So I think that’s that. I do my best, I still, of the people who leave the most space, of course Miles Davis and Wayne Shorter and those incredible, I still am trying to get to that place. Like if you see Wayne Shorter’s group play often he will just play a couple of notes and just like stand there for a long period of time. And it’s that whole time, like okay now what is he going to play. And it’s pretty special. So those memories of like okay, and you have this period of time, like I say. So you can fill up every space and like play all the technique you have but what does that mean? It’s like okay there’s a lot of other saxophone players who have way more technique than me. I feel like I have a decent amount of technique but I don’t need to show it all the time. So I try to think first of all the melody and I’m trying to, like my father, I’m trying to sing through the instrument, I’m trying to make it like just say a very well known song like that think about Ella or Sarah Vaughan or somebody singing it you know, like how would I sing this? You know?
